type: M10 PRE-REGISTRATION -- three robustness arms converting stated limitations into measurements
motivation: Three limitations were reported honestly rather than fixed: (2) the train-row cap, (3) datasets excluded because rotation is undefined on categorical data, (4) no Bayes oracle on real data. (4) is now addressed by re-analysis (regret against best-of-all models, results/m7_regret_vs_best.csv, no new compute). (2) could NOT be tested within M9 because most datasets sit exactly at the 1500-row cap, leaving no large-n half.

arm_A_scale.question: Does the rotation effect depend on training-set size?
arm_A_scale.design: rotation vs original at n_train in [500, 1500, 4000] on the 20 eligible datasets with the most rows; TabPFN only.
arm_A_scale.H_A: The paired degradation stays positive at EVERY n level (Wilcoxon one-sided per level, alpha=0.05). A positive Spearman(n_train, degradation) would mean the cap UNDERSTATES the effect, a negative one that it overstates it; both are reportable, and the pre-registered claim is only that the effect survives at all three levels.

arm_B_lowdim.question: Does the effect hold on the 11 datasets excluded only for having 2-3 numeric columns? Rotation is well defined in 2D.
arm_B_lowdim.design: identical to M9 with the eligibility rule lowered to >=2 numeric columns. Reported as a SEPARATE sample, never merged into the M9 primary or replication.
arm_B_lowdim.H_B: TabPFN degrades under rotation on these datasets (paired one-sided, alpha=0.05).

arm_C_categorical.question: 23 datasets have 0-1 numeric columns, so no rotation exists. Is there an information-preserving perturbation for them?
arm_C_categorical.design: randomly PERMUTE the integer codes of every categorical column. A relabelling is a bijection, so it preserves information exactly and leaves Bayes risk unchanged -- the categorical analogue of rotation. It destroys only the ORDINAL structure an ordinal encoding accidentally imposes.
arm_C_categorical.H_C: TabPFN's log-loss increases under code permutation (paired one-sided, alpha=0.05). This tests whether TabPFN exploits the arbitrary ordinality of ordinal-encoded categoricals, which would be a deployment-relevant bias in its own right.

analysis_plan: each arm reported separately with its own n
no arm is pooled into the M9 primary or replication results
directions and alpha are fixed here
